expectations.evidence: Section 2.2 lists all three levels in a table: BEGRÄNSAT HEMLIG (Restricted), HEMLIG (Secret), KVALIFICERAT HEMLIG (Top Secret), plus ÖPPEN.

Section 2.1 identifies Säkerhetsskyddslagen (2018:585) as the primary legal framework. Referenced throughout including Section 2.4 hierarchy, Section 7.2 export procedures, and Section 12.1 accreditation.
FMV and MUST are listed in Section 2.1 as accreditation authorities. Section 12 details the full accreditation lifecycle with FMV/MUST including driftgodkännande (operational approval).

Section 2.1 lists Säpo as managing personnel security clearance. Section 3.1 states all 12 cleared engineers hold HEMLIG-level clearance via Säpo. Risk register notes Säpo clearance process takes 6+ months.
Section 4.1 specifies SDIP-27 Zone B minimum TEMPEST requirements, mentions Zone A for high-sensitivity workloads, shielded room (Faraday cage), and red/black cabling separation per MUST guidance.
Section 3.1 explicitly states 12 HEMLIG-cleared engineers out of 40 total. Section 3.2 provides detailed team structure. Architectural implications (on-call, bus factor, vendor access) are discussed.

Section 2.3 states: 'HEMLIG data must remain within Swedish territory at all times. No cloud provider, no foreign data center, no cross-border replication.' Section 4.1 requires location within Sweden.

Section 4.2 states 'This is a true air gap. There is no network path from this environment to any unclassified network, the internet, or any lower-classification system.' Uses hardware data diodes for one-way import only.

Section 2.1 lists FRA as approving cryptographic products for classified use. Section 8.1 repeatedly references FRA-approved crypto modules. Section 2.4 places FRA crypto approvals as second in hierarchy of standards.

Section 7 details the full cross-domain data flow: data diode (Advenica SecuriCDS) for one-way import, manual media transfer with chain-of-custody, import scanning station, and formal downgrade/release for export.

RKE2 chosen partly for being FLOSS (Apache 2.0). Appendix A shows nearly all FLOSS stack. Section 16 notes FLOSS savings. Vault entry notes BSL license concern and suggests OpenBao as FLOSS fork. OpenShift acknowledged as alternative if CC certification needed.

Section 2.1 explicitly states 'not US DISA STIGs, not NIST 800-53, not FedRAMP' and that Swedish framework always takes precedence. Section 2.4 places NIST only as informative reference. All authorities and legal instruments are Swedish.
